doc.title: Ada Rovatti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 13, 2022

title: Remote recording workflow with Randy
summary: They record solos and horn parts from sent MP3s or WAV files at home, and she engineers.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: So it seems that you and Randy have found a way, and I suppose this maybe is just news to me, that there is technology now that you can exchange with people with sound files and okay this song needs a solo. So they send you — can you explain this process to me?

Yes. We get contacted to I would say put a solo or a horn arrangement or anything, and they just send sometimes just an MP3 if it’s already made a good mix. Sometimes we tend to ask for a different .WAV file so we can do our own mix to hear better the drums or whatever. And we just kind of — they send the charts, I map out the charts and record it. Sometimes they send already the Pro Tools files so it’s easy maybe to upload it. Sometimes it’s just the MP3 of the .WAV file and I’m the technician in the household. So I set up all the sessions for him, and then take a few takes, you know, clean it up if he’s doing a horn section he lays down all his parts and clean it up. And then I add my own parts and align with him just to be sure it’s nice and tight. And that’s it you know. It’s kind of a tailoring kind of job. And sometimes you send a couple, you know two or three solos just to be sure, so whoever produced the track hopefully one of the tracks will envision what they are looking for. You know, it happens sometimes they cut themselves a track and use half of one and half the other, but usually you know we send something that is already fluent and had a kind of a nice, you know, little speech. A little talk. A little story. You know? Because sometimes it happens that people that they cut themselves and it’s like oops, that was not a good cut. You know as a musician you know where you’re going and we recognize our little story and then if somebody cut it and put half and half you say that’s not where I was going for. So it’s interesting how we kind of know.
